chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abi al-Khattab, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Bashir, on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nadri, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
I heard him say: There are six characteristics which a believer does not have: poverty; being unknown; being stubborn; telling lies; being jealous and transgression of people’s rights.
ai.seo_question: What are the six characteristics that a believer does not have according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies six spiritual and behavioral deficiencies that characterize the absence of true faith, contrasting them with the noble traits of the *Mu'min*. This enumeration serves as a diagnostic tool in Shia ethics, linking internal states like jealousy (*hasad*) and stubbornness (*lajajah*) to external manifestations of faith, thereby guiding believers toward moral perfection (*kamal*).
